channel.title: Weekly Worker — Society & Culture (unofficial)
channel.description: Unofficial RSS feed of articles published by Weekly Worker — Society & Culture.

item.title: Health under attack
item.description: What lies behind the surge of measles cases in the USA? It is not just Donald Trump and his health secretary. James Linney blames the general environment of disinformation and distrust in science
item.dc:creator: James Linney

item.title: Time has run out
item.description: Antalya ended in complete failure. But the big victory scored by the oil producers and fossil fuel lobbyists underlines that the whole Cop merry-go-round has done nothing to halt the rise in global temperatures. Michael Roberts provides the damning facts and figures
item.dc:creator: Michael Roberts

item.title: Wholly Jewish in implementation?
item.description: It is not western Jewry that is to blame for the ongoing genocide in Gaza. To say otherwise is to mistake the symptoms for the disease, says Tony Greenstein in his open letter to Susan Abulhawa
item.dc:creator: Tony Greenstein

item.title: Socialism, gentrification and abjection
item.description: Paul Demarty reviews Fredrik deBoer All in your head Simon & Schuster 2026, pp291, £20
item.dc:creator: Paul Demarty

item.title: Turn fear into active use
item.description: Calls for public ownership and democratic control are all well and good, but what about now? The left needs to embrace AI and employ it for our own purposes. As a first step, says Yassamine Mather, we need to know how the technology works. After that we can develop, master and apply
item.dc:creator: Yassamine Mather

item.title: Celebrity culture in the dock
item.description: With the conviction of Russell Brand on one count of rape and three of sexual assault, and now the David Walliams allegations, Paul Demarty calls for self-critical reflection on the left and a healthier, more egalitarian sexual culture
item.dc:creator: Paul Demarty

item.title: Dancing the word
item.description: Jack Conrad reviews Chris Knight and Jerome Lewis The revolutionary origins of language New Haven CT 2026, pp384, hbk £25
item.dc:creator: Jack Conrad

item.title: Slavery’s imperial apologists
item.description: Charles Windsor has not apologised for Britain’s role in Caribbean slavery. Nor has Andy Burnham. Mike Macnair says the official arguments against apologies and reparations are bogus. But to really right the wrongs of the past requires the overthrow of the world capitalist order
item.dc:creator: Mike Macnair

item.title: Bertolt Brecht and Holy Joy
item.description: Culture can bring together theatre, poetry, music, stand-up comedy, anthropology and communist politics. That, explains Tam Dean Burn, is the ambition of the Diderot Gesellschaft Movement
item.dc:creator: Tam Dean Burn

item.title: Nature cannot go ignored
item.description: There are still those on the left who say ‘labour creates all wealth’. Seemingly militant, seemingly pro-worker, seemingly anti-capitalist, but profoundly wrong, says Jack Conrad
item.dc:creator: Jack Conrad

item.title: New age of security chaos
item.description: PHP2Shell is the latest of many disastrous security vulnerabilities. Their discovery and exploitation are easier than ever in the age of AI. Buckle up, advises Paul Demarty
item.dc:creator: Paul Demarty

item.title: Banking on moonshots
item.description: Much to the alarm of the AI industry and interested governments, data centres face a growing tide of local opposition. Is this a reactionary attempt to roll back progress or a defensible popular revolt? Paul Demarty investigates
item.dc:creator: Paul Demarty

item.title: Seven you need to watch
item.description: Over 200 feature films and shorts were showcased over October 7-18 at the 70th annual London Film Festival. As with every year, there were some duds, a few shocks, but many treats. Jim Moody picks his particular highlights
item.dc:creator: Jim Moody

item.title: Postcard from the future
item.description: A Godzilla El Niño could persist until at least early next year, bringing record temperatures along with more flooding and drought. But there is also a possibility, paradoxically, that it could trigger a deep freeze in Europe, writes Eddie Ford
item.dc:creator: Eddie Ford

item.title: Why Israel is a racist state
item.description: We reprint this article by Moshé Machover in light of the media-amplified campaign against Green Party activists for daring to categorise Zionism as a form of racism. It most certainly is. As with any colonial-settler project, Zionism involves systemic discrimination against the indigenous population. First published in September 2018 by Labour Party Marxists
item.dc:creator: Moshe Machover

item.title: Straight from the playbook
item.description: Media-amplified outrage over the A105 ‘Zionism is racism’ motion has nothing to do with anti-Semitism, argues Carla Roberts. It is about imposing imperialist interests on a potential junior coalition partner
item.dc:creator: Carla Roberts

item.title: Guilty on all charges
item.description: Man City systematically inflated revenues and reduced costs to hide the owner spending some £830 million to buy success on the field. What does this say about top-flight football? Carl Collins gives some compelling answers
item.dc:creator: Carl Collins

item.title: In their thousands, insects
item.description: Blood sucking flies, mosquitoes, ticks, fleas and other bugs are spreading diseases once confined to the tropics and subtropics. James Linney says the blame lies squarely with climate change and a system blinded by production for the sake of production
item.dc:creator: James Linney

item.title: Publish the report in full
item.description: In what could be the stirrings of climate socialism the JIC security chiefs are warning of apocalyptic dangers, writes Eddie Ford. We demand complete openness on such matters. The public need to know what the government does not want the public to know
item.dc:creator: Eddie Ford

item.title: Charles vs Charles
item.description: Today’s royal family is a load-bearing institution of the capitalist state, its fate inseparable from the continuity of that state. It will not be brought down by this or that scandal, let alone an embittered former brother-in-law bent on revenge, says Paul Demarty
item.dc:creator: Paul Demarty

item.title: Politics of apolitical culture
item.description: Saying sorry over Gaza and pleasing no-one. Behind Ed Sheeran’s unconvincing apologies there lies a complex network of commercial interests, political pressures and institutional power, writes Carl Collins
item.dc:creator: Carl Collins

item.title: The few and the many
item.description: Mega-donations are not the only way to gain access and influence - there is also the role played by the media, think-tanks, schools, universities and charities. We need to build our own class institutions along with the necessary finances, argues Eddie Ford
item.dc:creator: Eddie Ford

item.title: Angel or McGuffin?
item.description: Jacob Coxon’s very public resignation from Anthropic has once again raised the spectre of the AI apocalypse. But which AI apocalypse? Paul Demarty weighs up the risks to humanity
item.dc:creator: Paul Demarty

item.title: Coping with the crisis
item.description: Deadly heatwaves, devastating wildfires and terrible floods - and El Niño has not even reached its peak. Communists say we need extreme measures if we are to avoid climate catastrophe, writes Eddie Ford
item.dc:creator: Eddie Ford

item.title: Not all about profit
item.description: Football attracts millions of devoted followers. Yet, when it comes to the bottom line, many clubs show regular losses. Despite that, narrow-minded left commentators regularly complain that money and the pursuit of profit is ruining the beautiful game. It is more complex than that, writes Carl Collins
item.dc:creator: Carl Collins

item.title: War is always hell
item.description: Mike Belbin reviews Christopher Nolan (writer and director) The Odyssey 2026, general release
item.dc:creator: Mike Belbin

item.title: When cybercabs kill
item.description: Pilot tests are already ongoing and commercially available, fully autonomous vehicles are expected on UK roads by the second half of 2027. But what happens when there is a crash, when someone dies? Legal rules will protect the capitalists, suggests Mike Macnair
item.dc:creator: Mike Macnair

item.title: Money talks to money
item.description: Despite the financial scandals, pushback from the liberal establishment and reduced polling numbers, in Birmingham Nigel Farage reached out to the capitalist class, writes Eddie Ford
item.dc:creator: Eddie Ford

item.title: Racing towards general intelligence
item.description: We have already had the Hugging Face incident. Whether AI is used to expand human capabilities or to wipe us out will be decided by politics, ultimately by the politics of class against class, says Yassamine Mather
item.dc:creator: Yassamine Mather

item.title: Abundance for all
item.description: How can climate catastrophe be stopped? Capitalism, almost by definition, depends on endless accumulation and the production of more and more stuff. But, at CU 2026, Ted Reese argued that degrowth is not the answer
item.dc:creator: Ted Reese
